The solution states that $f(b) = 8$ implies $b^2 + 8 = 16$. This is wrong.

If $f(b) = 8$ and $f(x) = x^2 + 8$, then:
$$b^2 + 8 = 8$$

not $b^2 + 8 = 16$.

The solution incorrectly set $b^2 + 8 = 16$, which would only be true if $f(b) = 16$.

From the incorrect $b^2 + 8 = 16$, subtracting 8 gives $b^2 = 8$, not $0$. This is the arithmetic consequence of the first error, so the student carries the wrong intermediate value forward.
